title: Hario Switch brewing guide
scope: Original glass Switch 02 SSD-200-B, using the manual's 20 g coffee / approximately 240 mL input-water steep-and-release procedure. Rinsing follows Hario's compatible V60-paper instructions; starting the approximate two-minute steep after filling is an explicit editorial clock clarification. Glass 03, hybrid and continuously open variants are separate notes.

sources.title: Immersion Dripper SWITCH SSD-200 instruction manual
supports: 20 g medium-ground coffee, approximately 240 mL hot input water, approximately two-minute steep, then release; no numeric brewing-water temperature or total-time deadline.
02 paper; raised lever retains water; lever flat with base drains and stays released; approximately 200 mL finished-capacity label.

Gentle pressing, stable server placement before filling, no touching/carrying after hot water is added, ball retention, secure glass seating, gloves for disassembly, nonabrasive cleaning and dishwasher permission.

sources.title: V60 SWITCH Glass Dripper
supports: Glass SSD-200-B is listed as 200 mL finished capacity; SSD-360-B as 360 mL capacity, without an explicit safe maximum closed-fill quantity.
Switch supports V60-style flowing use and immersion; heatproof glass bowl, silicone base, PCT resin switch and stainless-steel ball.

sources.title: V60 Glass Switch Immersion Dripper product information
supports: 02 and 03 glass versions are supplied with matching 02 and 03 V60 paper respectively; listed capacities 200 and 360 mL.
PCT resin lever, silicone base and stainless-steel ball. The page's ceramic heading conflicts with its glass product text and is not used as material evidence.

sources.title: Intermediate V60 Brew Guide
supports: Rinse V60 02 paper and discard rinse water; weigh 15 g coffee and tare; 92–96°C, approximately 30-second bloom, circular pour until scale reads 250 g.
Approximately 2.5-minute drainage language is contextual rather than a guaranteed Switch completion time; header says 250 mL but operational pour target explicitly says 250 g.

sources.title: Ole Kristian Bøen's Switch Recipe
sources.author_or_organization: Ole Kristian Bøen, published by HARIO Europe
supports: Switch 02, 16.5 g medium-fine coffee, 96°C water and 3:00–3:15 expected total time.
Closed 50 g bloom for 40 seconds; open and add 100 g centrally; close at 1:30 and add 90 g circularly; release at 2:10. Explicit mass additions sum to 240 g, while header states 240 mL.

sources.title: How to Brew with the Hario V60 Switch: verified recipe text
supports: A distinct September 18, 2026 regional recipe states 15 g medium coffee, 250 g water at 92–94°C, closed 50 g bloom for 30 seconds, fill to 250 g and release at a two-minute mark. Its opening paragraph says 92°C.
The text is verified as published; conflicting clock descriptions, universal capacity and extraction explanations are not adopted as verified hardware or scientific claims.

sources.title: How to Brew with the Hario V60 Switch: unresolved specifications and explanations
supports: Evidence of an unresolved publication conflict only: the article calls two minutes closed steeping while its staged recipe blooms first and releases at two minutes; its about-300-mL cone assertion lacks a precise model/fill basis.
No support claimed for universal immunity to over-extraction, mandatory coarse grind, a lid on the original glass Switch, or a universal safe 300 mL fill.

recipe.name: Hario Switch 02 manual steep-and-release
equipment: Original glass Hario Switch 02 SSD-200-B, assembled with ball and movable lever
Stable heat-safe server with adequate room for the brew
Heat-safe graduated vessel for the approximately 240 mL input-water example
recipe.quantity_precision: 240 mL is approximate input volume. 12 mL/g is volume per mass, not a mass-based 1:12 ratio. The manual's approximately 200 mL finished-capacity label is not an exact beverage target.

water_temperature_c.control: user; manual specifies hot water without a measured target

recipe.grind_description: Medium grind as the manual's English text states; Japanese text describes medium-fine. No exact grinder setting is established.

expected_time_s.clock_start: First brew water touches the coffee; separate approximate 120-second steep countdown starts when filling is complete
expected_time_s.clock_end: Standing water is gone and continuous drainage has become occasional drops

recipe.completion_signal: No standing water above the bed and continuous flow has diminished to occasional drops; leave the hot brewer in place until safe to handle.

steps.instruction: Place the assembled Switch 02 on its server. Fold the 02 paper seam, fit the cone, rinse with hot water with the lever flat/open, then discard drained rinse water.
steps.why: Wet the paper and warm the server before brewing.
steps.completion: Paper seated and wet; rinse drained and discarded; brewer stable.

steps.instruction: Raise the lever to close the valve and add 20 g medium-ground coffee.
steps.why: The raised lever allows the ball to seal the outlet and retain brew water.

steps.instruction: Pour approximately 240 mL hot water over the grounds, keeping liquid below the paper top and leaving the brewer on its server. Begin the separate total-time log at first water.
steps.why: The closed valve retains the brew for immersion.
steps.completion: Recipe water added and grounds wet; no overflow or unintended leakage.

steps.instruction: After filling, start an approximately two-minute steep countdown. Leave the valve closed; optional stirring is omitted from this first-brew path.
steps.why: This follows the manual's pour-then-steep order using an explicit editorial countdown origin.
steps.time_precision: approximate; measured from filling completion, not total brew elapsed
steps.completion: Approximately two minutes of post-fill steeping elapsed.

steps.instruction: Press the lever gently until it lies flat with the base to open the valve. Keep the filled hot brewer in place.
steps.why: Opening releases coffee through the paper into the server; the lever stays open without continued finger pressure.
steps.completion: Coffee flows into the server; brewer remains stable.

steps.instruction: Observe until standing water is gone and continuous drainage has become occasional drops. Wait until safe to handle before removing the hot brewer; serve from the server.
steps.why: Drainage depends on coffee, grind and paper, so a fixed timer cannot establish completion.
steps.completion: No standing water and no continuous stream; hot glass is handled only when safe.

variants.name: Weighed-water adaptation of the manual
variants.how_it_differs: Using 20 g coffee and 240 g input water is a convenient mass-based 1:12 adaptation; it must not be presented as the manual's literal approximately 240 mL wording. No temperature or exact beverage yield is added.

variants.name: Ole Kristian Bøen's Switch 02 hybrid
variants.how_it_differs: 16.5 g medium-fine coffee at 96°C; first-water clock. Closed 50 g bloom to 40 s; open and add 100 g centrally to 150 g; at 90 s close and add 90 g circularly to 240 g; release at 130 s; expected completion 180–195 s, observing drainage. Published heading says 240 mL but the explicit pours sum to 240 g.

variants.name: Switch 02 kept open for V60 gravity brewing
variants.how_it_differs: Valve stays flat/open from rinse through completion. Use Hario's separate 15 g/250 g V60 operation, 92–96°C, approximately 30-second bloom and small circular pouring; confirm drainage rather than imposing an immersion release.

variants.name: Larger original glass Switch 03
variants.how_it_differs: 03 is advertised at 360 mL capacity and comes with matching 03 V60 paper. A larger closed fill needs capacity/headroom and drainage checks; neither 360 mL nor a V60 cup-count rating establishes a universal input-water amount.

troubleshooting.symptom: Water escapes while the lever is raised
troubleshooting.check_first: After cooling, check that the ball is present, the glass sits securely in the base and the lever moves correctly.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Reassemble according to the manual with gloves; check retention over the server before brewing again. Replace damaged parts rather than forcing the valve.

troubleshooting.check_first: Confirm the lever is flat/open, paper is correctly seated and the cooled outlet assembly is clear and correctly assembled.
troubleshooting.adjustment: After equipment checks, try a slightly coarser grind with the same dose and water; compare taste and flow. No universal drainage deadline is established.

troubleshooting.check_first: Confirm measured coffee and input water, full wetting, and the intended post-fill steep rather than an accidentally open valve.
troubleshooting.adjustment: App-authored taste suggestion: try a slightly longer steep or slightly finer grind, one variable at a time. Bean and water differences can also affect taste.

troubleshooting.check_first: Check that steeping was not prolonged unintentionally and that excess agitation or drainage restriction did not change the procedure.
troubleshooting.adjustment: App-authored taste suggestion: try a shorter steep or a slightly coarser grind, changing one variable at a time. Do not infer extraction percentage from taste alone.

safety: Set the brewer securely on a stable server or drip stand before adding hot water; do not touch or carry the filled hot dripper. Leave it in place until drained and safe to handle.
Press the lever gently; excessive force can overturn the brewer and spill hot liquid.
Do not use cracked, chipped or deeply scratched glass, or strike/scrape it with metal utensils. Avoid sudden cooling of hot glass or wet/cold contact that can cause thermal shock.
After cooling, clean with neutral detergent and a soft nonabrasive sponge. The manual allows dishwasher use subject to the dishwasher's instructions.

Keep the removable stainless-steel ball from being lost during washing. Wear gloves when detaching or attaching the glass and base, follow the assembly diagram, reseat securely and confirm lever movement before reuse.
Keep the brewer away from children; do not add water past the paper's top or assume advertised capacity is a safe brim-fill allowance.

app_audit.finding: switch_official_20_240 sets inputG=240 and ratioValue=12 with OFFICIAL_PROCEDURE/HIGH attribution, and time=range(150,180). The manual specifies approximately 240 mL and approximately two-minute steeping, without that total-time range. HOT_UNSPECIFIED and unresolved beverage output are correctly retained.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Preserve the source record, but describe the runtime 240 g target as a weighed app adaptation, or model the original volume directly. Keep steep duration distinct from total completion and remove unsupported source attribution for the 150–180 s total window.

app_audit.finding: The official plan starts ADD_WATER at brew elapsed 0, follows it with a 120 s steep countdown, but gives RELEASE a brew-elapsed start target of exactly 120 s. Those cues conflict whenever filling takes time, and the manual's approximate timing is typed as EXACT.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Choose and expose one clock convention. For the manual's pour-then-steep order, time approximately 120 s from fill completion and do not add an incompatible fixed elapsed-release target. Keep observation-based drawdown.

app_audit.finding: The loaded immutable projection says Add 20 g coffee and 240 g water, Steep for 2:00 after the preceding stage, then release At 2:00. It also says drawdown is usually under about one minute. The projection is consumed by P1ExactGuidanceCatalog; current factual errata has no Switch branch.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Keep immutable provenance intact. Correct live guidance through a reviewed adapter/erratum to label mass adaptation, distinguish steep and elapsed clocks, avoid unsupported drainage deadlines, and retain the observable finish cue.

app_audit.finding: The Bøen typed plan correctly uses 50/100/90 g additions, cumulative 50/150/240 g, 96°C, open-pour start 40 s, close/final pour 90 s, release 130 s and expected finish 180–195 s. Projected guidance explicitly re-closes the valve for the final pour.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Preserve the sequence and source-stage identity; explain first-water timing and hybrid phases. Add current direct Hario Europe attribution while retaining the historical SRC-KURASU-SWITCH provenance; do not merge with the simple manual baseline.

app_audit.finding: switch_gravity_15_250 uses a 30 s approximate bloom, 92–96°C, cumulative 250 g and observation-based drawdown with 150 s only a STARTING_POINT. Projected guidance says lever open throughout. This is consistent with the separate V60 operation, not the immersion manual.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Preserve continuously open behavior and contextual timing. Display it as V60-style gravity use of the Switch with its separate source, not as the official Switch immersion recipe.

app_audit.finding: Shared Switch guidance says close/open the valve without describing up versus flat positions. Safety copy covers stability and hot glass, but omits the manual's gentle-press, missing-ball and cooled assembly checks.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Add concise up=closed and flat=draining cues; place gentle pressing and no carrying while hot at the relevant action, with assembly/ball checks in troubleshooting and cleanup detail.

app_audit.finding: The generic steep-and-release defaults also used by hario_switch are 1:16, 90–96°C and 120–240 s, with BrewWaterMinusRetention(2.0 g/g) explicitly an estimated output model. These differ from the named manual and Bøen recipes.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Keep generic defaults visibly distinct from named recipes. Retain estimate labeling and an unresolved/measured output path; do not promote 2.0 g/g to a brewer-specific physical fact or fixed yield guarantee.

app_audit.finding: No Hario Switch enum entry exists in the everyday BrewMethod registry, despite profile/exact-catalog entries. app/src/main/assets/grinders.json also has no Switch-specific entry.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Document this support boundary. Any future everyday-method integration needs recipe/workflow, filter-size and unit decisions; catalog presence does not prove localization or exact grinder settings.

app_audit.finding: The prior audit calls the 20 g/240 g official recipe a match and confirms approximately two-minute steeping, but does not note the manual's approximately 240 mL quantity or current clock conflict. Bøen and open-switch distinctions remain correct.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Append current evidence clarifying units and timing while preserving the historical audit's date and scope; do not claim the named variants were absent or already corrected by Switch-specific factual errata.

uncertainties: The original manual's English grind description is medium; its Japanese wording is medium-fine. This is a starting texture, not a calibrated grinder setting.
The manual does not define timer-zero as first-water contact. The guide explicitly uses approximately two minutes after filling and leaves total brew duration unknown.

The 02 approximately 200 mL label concerns finished capacity; 03 is listed at 360 mL capacity by current US product text, whose wording does not define a universal safe closed-fill limit. Exact beverage yield and absorption are unverified.
The current Hario.com manual link returned HTTP 403; an original Hario-hosted manual at hario.cc was fully readable. Revision equivalence of the inaccessible current link is unverified.
The historical Kurasu URL could not be read. Bøen's direct Hario Europe recipe was fully read; its heading uses mL while explicit pours use g.

The current Hario UK Switch article is verified as published but mixes two-minute steeping with a bloom-first/two-minute elapsed release, presents an unqualified about-300-mL cone capacity and suggests a lid. Those statements are not used to define the original glass brewer's hardware or this baseline.
The 2025 English catalog exceeded the web tool's size limit; a purported Hario catalog mirror at ibodr.com timed out. No search-snippet-only capacity facts are treated as verified.

Taste-adjustment directions and the no-standing-water/intermittent-drop completion wording are app-authored practical explanations consistent with adjustable grind/steep and observed drainage, not universal extraction diagnostics.
This is English research content. No physical brewing, Android device execution, release validation or translation approval was performed.
do_not_claim: The manual prescribes exact 240 g input, a mass-based 1:12 ratio, 96°C, or a fixed total finish deadline.
The approximate two-minute steep is the entire brew including filling and drainage.
20 g/approximately 240 mL, Bøen's hybrid and 15 g/250 g open-switch V60 use are one interchangeable recipe.
02 always holds a safe 300 mL closed fill, 03's 360 mL rating is a precise input target, or every large batch can be doubled unchanged.
A specific grinder number, exact beverage yield, universal 2 g/g retention or decaf time shortcut is established.
Immersion cannot over-extract, bitterness always means too-fine grind, or one-minute drainage proves correctness.
The raised lever opens the valve, the lever must be held while draining, or the filled hot brewer can be lifted/swirl-carried safely.
Exact-catalog entries establish everyday BrewMethod, localized or physically brewed support.
